metadata.title: How to Sign In with Okta Using Capacitor
metadata.description: Connect Okta to a Capacitor 8 app with OIDC and PKCE: create the native app integration, set redirect URIs, refresh tokens, logout, and fix Okta errors.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu

faq.question: Do I need an Okta client secret for a Capacitor app?
faq.answer: No. Create an OIDC Native Application, which is a public client. Client authentication is set to None and PKCE protects the code exchange. A secret shipped in an app bundle is not a secret.

faq.question: Which Okta issuer URL should I use?
faq.answer: Use a custom authorization server issuer such as https://your-org.okta.com/oauth2/default when your own API validates the access tokens. The org authorization server (https://your-org.okta.com) only issues access tokens for Okta's own APIs, so your backend cannot validate them.

faq.question: How do I get a refresh token from Okta?
faq.answer: Enable the Refresh Token grant type on the app integration, request the offline_access scope, and make sure the access policy rule on your authorization server allows the refresh token grant. Okta can rotate refresh tokens on every use, so save the new one each time.

faq.question: Why do users get 'User is not assigned to the client application'?
faq.answer: Okta only lets assigned users or groups sign in to an app integration. Open the app in the Admin Console, go to Assignments, and assign the users or a group such as Everyone.

How Okta login works in a Capacitor app

Your app never shows a password form. It opens the Okta sign-in page in a secure browser, Okta handles MFA and policies, then redirects back to your app with a code. The app exchanges the code plus the PKCE verifier for tokens.
